counterfactual_missing_items: Histopathologic confirmation of the fat-density lesion as a lipoma is absent
The raw vignette does not explicitly state that the mass is the 'leading mass' of the intussusception
No surgical or biopsy pathology is provided to confirm the lead point
decisive_items: Contrast-enhanced CT of the abdomen demonstrated a well-defined hypodense lesion measuring 4.6 × 3.4 cm with fat density in the sigmoid-colon wall protruding into the lumen, along with invagination of the descending colon into the sigmoid colon consistent with intussusception
Colonoscopy revealed a 5 × 5 cm exophytic mass at the descending–sigmoid junction occupying half of the lumen
response.rationale: C1 is the only candidate that integrates both the CT-confirmed intussusception and the fat-density intraluminal lesion as a leading mass, matching the adult intussusception pattern. R6 captures the intussusception but omits the lead-point etiology; R8 is a generic mass label; R2 is contradicted by fat density and normal CEA; R1 and R7 rely only on nonspecific inflammatory symptoms and ignore the decisive imaging.

rejected.why: Only nonspecific mucosal inflammation/discharge; cannot explain the CT fat-density lesion and intussusception.
Exophytic mass alone could suggest cancer, but CT fat density and normal CEA favor a benign leading mass.
Generic 'polyp or mass' misses the definitive intussusception and fat-density lead point.
Symptoms are nonspecific; no diverticula or pericolic inflammation is present on CT.
